chunks: Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Alawi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim informed us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Adhinah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

In His Word, the Mighty and High: 'No secret counsel of three is there but He is the fourth of them, nor of five but He is the sixth of them, nor of fewer than that nor more but He is with them wherever they are.'

He said: He is One, Unique in Essence, distinct from His creation, and with this He described Himself. He encompasses all things by supervision, encompassing, and power. Nothing is hidden from Him, not even the weight of an atom in the heavens or the earth, nor smaller or larger than that, by encompassing and knowledge, not by Essence.
Because spaces are limited, enclosed by four boundaries. If He were by Essence, it would be necessary for Him to be enclosed.
ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq explain Allah's presence in the verse 'He is with them wherever they are'?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the theological nuance in Surah Al-Mujadila by distinguishing between Allah's essential presence (which would imply spatial confinement) and His presence by knowledge and power, affirming His transcendence beyond the four boundaries of space. This interpretation aligns with the Shia doctrine of *Tanzih* (divine transcendence), emphasizing that God is not a body occupying a place but is omnipresent through His attributes. The hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding how the Divine can be 'with' creation without being mixed with it or limited by physical dimensions.
